historical_endpoint.rule: Working historical corpus cutoff is 1949-12-31 for mainland-era Republic central-government episodes. Post-1949 PRC/ROC political leadership is deliberately a separate modern-leadership dataset, not silently appended to an imperial/historical ruler corpus.
historical_endpoint.reason: Prevents an open-ended current-politics list while preserving the complete late-imperial→Republic historical transition.

principles: Republic-era inclusion is office/episode based and politically neutral: a person enters only for a formal or de facto supreme central-government episode satisfying the common ruler rule.
Ordinary regional warlord command is not enough. Zhang Zuolin qualifies through the 1927-1928 Beijing military-government head-of-state episode, not simply because he led the Fengtian clique.
Short acting heads are retained for maximal-set completeness but can be LIMITED-EVIDENCE for cognitive distillation.
Collective governments with no unique supreme office are represented as institutional episodes rather than arbitrarily inventing a single 'ruler'.
Foreign-sponsored regimes with heavily constrained sovereignty are tracked as EXTENDED rather than normalized into CORE.

exclusions_and_edges.reason: Regional military command without a qualifying central-government supreme office is not enough.
A committee is modeled as an institutional episode; members are not automatically person-level rulers.
Separate modern political leadership dataset under working historical cutoff; avoids mixing current politics into the ruler-corpus denominator.
